title: Claude Max Workflow: How to Set One Up (2026 Guide)
summary: A Claude Max workflow routes work between models and defines resets when limits hit. Build handoffs using manual notes or automation tools.
body_markdown:
## Automating the hand-offs around Claude with Activepieces


The usage window that limits Claude is out of Activepieces' reach, but it does automate the steps that surround Claude (receiving the brief, filing the draft, notifying the client, logging the deadline), and a run of those hand-offs costs 1 credit however many steps it has.


That boundary decides what to hand it.


In the Activepieces flow builder, an Agent step sits next to the deterministic filing, notifying and logging steps inside one flow.


The run trace for a single brief then shows one execution, from the brief arriving to the deadline being written down, with no webhook joining two products. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production, and the core is MIT-licensed.


When a draft goes missing mid-morning, that one trace is where you look.


### What to automate and what to leave manual


If a person does a step the same way every time and no judgment is involved, it belongs in the automation. That is the test for any step.


Moving a brief from an inbox or form into a working folder passes. So does saving the finished draft to the right client folder, sending the "draft ready" message, and writing the deadline into a tracker.


Each is a hand-off, and hand-offs are where work gets dropped when a session runs out mid-task.


Leave manual anything that needs a decision. Whether a draft is good enough to send is one. Whether to spend the remaining window on this client or the next is another.


Switching to the named fallback when the window closes also stays with a person, because the routine you wrote says who does it, and a flow can't see that you're out of room.


Be clear about one limit.[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) doesn't raise Claude Max limits. Its own meter is separate: the Free plan gives 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows.


If a step calls Claude through the API rather than through your Max session, that use is billed separately from Max. Check Anthropic's pricing page before you build it, because it changes what the flow costs.


### How the workflow is built


Left to right, the flow runs: brief arrives, Claude drafts, draft filed, client notified, deadline logged. The illustration below shows the flow wrapping the outer hand-offs, with Claude as a separate box that has its own usage meter.


What to take from it is that the meter sits outside the automation. A flow can start a run, but it can't refill the window the draft step draws on.


Build it in that order. Test each hand-off with an input that has broken things before: a brief with an attachment, a client name with an accent, a deadline with no date. A flow that works on a tidy demo brief proves nothing.


Next, keep the Claude step easy to pull out. When the window closes, that one box should be replaceable by the fallback, while the filing, notifying and logging around it keep running unchanged.
